text:
maria: quick follow-up from the cutover RFC — I'm proposing a lightweight lease-coordination API for proxies/control-plane so we can make cutovers deterministic without operator manual steps. wanted to surface tradeoffs.
aj: sounds good, what's the minimal contract?
maria: minimal is 3 endpoints: POST /lease/request, POST /lease/relinquish, GET /lease/status. leases are short-lived (sane default 30s) and heartbeating is optional. proxies only ask for a lease when preparing to serve resident-tenants during cutover.
jonathan: are leases per-tenant or per-proxy? per-shard?
maria: per-tenant+shard id. shard-level lets us batch but we keep tenant affinity in the token. per-tenant would be too many objects in control plane for large customers.
kate: what's the safety if control plane is slow? proxy can't block traffic indefinitely.
maria: good point — proxies must fall back to "serve-read-only" or forward to a fallback region after a short local timeout (we propose 200ms). lease acquisition is opportunistic; operator tooling shows mismatch alerts.
devin: how do we make cutover idempotent? two proxies could race to acquire the same lease during split-brain window.
maria: server side will use monotonic lease generation + compare-and-swap on metadata. acquisition response contains a lease_id and sequence number. proxy uses lease_id in subsequent HEADERS: `X-Region-Lease: <lease_id>` so control plane can validate. example payload: ```json
{"tenant_id":"t-123","shard":"s-4","requested_ttl_secs":30}
``` 
aj: love the header idea. but if control plane can't talk to the datastore, do we default-deny? that's risky for availability.
jonathan: tradeoff: default-allow increases risk of residency leakage. default-deny increases 5xx/latency during control-plane partitions. maybe a tiered policy: enterprise tenants can choose "allow-on-control-plane-fail" or strict. default for hosted customers should be conservative (deny).
kate: operator UX: we need a dashboard that correlates lease churn with traffic spikes + a "safety score" metric before a cutover.
devin: also expose metrics: lease_request_latency, lease_conflicts, lease_acquired_count, lease_grace_expirations.
maria: agreed. and add an audit log stream (append-only) so we can replay who requested what. retention 90 days.
aj: implementation question: where does the lease live? redis vs strongly-consistent kv?
maria: prefer strongly-consistent kv (etcd style) for correctness but we can have a short lived cache for performance. the write path must be linearizable for acquisition.
devin: can we optimize by giving proxies a signed token that represents a batch of leases (prefix cache)? reduces control plane trips for warm handoffs.
maria: yes — introduce a signed lease-bundle token with expiry and allowed-shards. proxies present bundle and only refresh when near expiry. security audit required.
jonathan: during canary cutovers we need a safe rollback. proposal: keep old proxies with their leases valid for an additional warm period (grace 60s) and route a % of traffic to previous region until metrics stable.
kate: how does this interact with KV cache ownership and writes? we need a clear demarcation: lease==write-authority. reads can be served if data-consent flags allow.
maria: write-authority mapped to lease. proxies check header `X-Write-Authority: lease_id` before accepting writes; failing that they forward to leader.
aj: any concerns about attack surface? signed tokens + short TTL reduces replay, but we should bind to proxy id and origin IP.
devin: +1 on binding. also add a revocation endpoint `POST /lease/revoke` for operator emergency.
maria: plan for rollout: 1) API + metrics + audit, internal canary 2) proxy opt-in with bundle tokens 3) expose tenant policy toggle 4) enable default-deny for a small percent 5) ramp.
jonathan: timeline?
maria: aiming for prototype end of sprint (2 weeks). need eng-runtime to wire header checks, eng-ml not involved.
kate: I'll add a brief runbook for rollback and operator commands. can we also include a health-check probe that returns active lease count?
maria: yes — GET /lease/health returns counts and last-applied-index. lightweight.
deploy-bot: deployment started: `lease-api-service v0.1.0` to staging at 1718054500
aj: looking at the staging logs — a couple of transient 409s when two proxies raced. that's expected, we'll treat as normal and retry with backoff.
devin: add jittered exponential backoff with cap 3 attempts.
maria: agreed. final ask: @aj please prototype the token signing format, @devin add the metrics + revocation endpoint, @kate write the runbook snippets. I'll collate in the RFC follow-up doc. :thumbsup:
